audit_notes: Slip length: Ybert et al. (2007) for posts, b/L = 0.325/sqrt(phi_s) - 0.44 = 1.028 - 0.44 = 0.59 -> b = 5.9 um, matches 6 um; b+ = 6/5.4 = 1.1. The pipeline may substitute simulation_coefficient for effective_slip_length; both are 6e-6 m. Net virtual-origin shift with the isotropic-slip penalty 0.35: 3.9 um -> expected gain b_net/(delta+b_net) = 3.9/98.9 = 3.9%. Meniscus stability: post size a = L*sqrt(phi_s) = 3.2 um, gap 6.8 um; Laplace breakthrough pressure ~ 2 gamma |cos theta_a| / gap = 2*0.072*0.5/6.8e-6 ~ 10.6 kPa. Turbulent wall pressure fluctuations p_rms ~ 2.5-3 tau_w = 125-150 Pa, peaks ~1 kPa: acceptable. Hydrostatic head varies 0-100 kPa over a 10 m draft, so a single 20 kPa supply overpressure cannot balance the whole hull: the manifold must be zoned by depth (every ~1 m, +-10 kPa), otherwise gas bubbles out near the waterline and the plastron floods at depth. Gas consumption by dissolution: k_L ~ 0.08 u_tau Sc^-2/3 = 0.08*0.221/63 = 2.8e-4 m/s, excess gas concentration ~0.015 m3/m3 per bar -> ~4e-6 m3/(s m2) at 1 bar excess, i.e. ~0.04 m3/s for 1e4 m2: small compressor duty. Structural: PDMS/ silica posts 3 um wide, ~5-10 um tall, fine under 50 Pa shear; membrane (ePTFE) mechanically fragile against abrasion and impacts; biofouling of the membrane pores is the main durability issue, not a safety issue. Baseline: same smooth FR wall with no gas (slip 0).
